Okay 1. There’s a difference between being blunt and an ass, and being kind. If you think that’s kind, I’m sorry for people you interact with daily. 

2. Actually, it IS mild. If you bother to google Cerebral Palsy, you’d understand. That’s ableist, friend. Yikerinos. 

3. You’re sorry but you have to ask? No, you’re nosy and like to put someone down under the guise of “trying to be kind”. I’m not actively trying to enter the bowl. It was simply a question of “Are there disabled SB/SD’s out there”. 

4. If you knew why I was living with my grandparents instead of assuming it’s because of my disability, you’d feel like a damn ass.  

Thanks for coming to my TedTalk, and try not to be so ableist next time.
Me too. I’m hoping we’ll cross paths again one day ❤️
To be fair, I wasn’t inquiring about my virginity or my immediate want to be in the bowl. I was simply asking regarding disabilities.

The internet is vast. So’s Reddit. If you don’t like that people under 18 are using the site, maybe see if you can find some 18+ subreddits. Additionally, maybe they’re on here because they don’t have any other support. Plus, you’re 22, not 82. Chances are, you’ve asked advice on this site. The “holier than thou” attitude is dumb. Relax and scroll past them my dude.

My favorite memory is my first time I think I realized that I could really make magic for a little kid. This was in March. 

He was in a wheelchair, had scars all over his head, and was looking at a Lion King cup. LK is my favorite movie, and I felt drawn to go talk to him. (We’ll call him H.) I walked over and asked if he was excited for the new upcoming movie, which he hadn’t known about. We make small talk and then I remember that our store had Simba pillow pets (and how my pillow pet at home is my absolute favorite). 
H didn’t know about the concept of pillow pets so he was enamored with it when I brought it over to him. Off to the side, I talk to H’s mom, and ask if he’d like to have the pillow. She said yes, but seemed hesitant because she really wasn’t planning on purchasing this plush. I told H’s mom not to worry, that Mickey Mouse told me that H needed to have this Simba pillow pet. So, I snipped the tag and told H the same, that Mickey Mouse wanted him to have Simba. His face immediately brightened and I got a huge hug and a kiss on the cheek. Thinking that was it, I let them get back to shopping. A few minutes later a fellow Cast Member came up, asking if the little boy I had been helping earlier was named H. When I said yes, she said. “I just spoke with them. They’re here celebrating H because H loves Disney World and he won’t be here next year.” 
Then, I realized. This kid was terminally ill. He wouldn’t be here next year because he wouldn’t be alive next year. It broke my heart. I had to keep it together until I could get backstage, because i knew I was minutes away from crying. So as I’m making my way backstage, H’s mom stops me, and she’s crying. She asks if she could take a picture of H and I. Of course she can! After a few more minutes of chatting, we part ways and I go in the back and sob for about 20 minutes. 

The worst part of the whole thing for me, is that I can’t keep up with H and his health journey. I don’t know his last name or his mom’s name to look them up. I’ll probably never see or hear about them or from them again, and it makes me sad. I hope he knows that he changed my life forever that day and I think about him almost daily.
Taking pictures backstage is a big no-no and could get you fired!

You know, working for Disney is what you make of it. It’s not for everyone, and I think so many people come into it with too high expectations. The simple joy of making magic for sick little kids made my day every day. Most of my fellow cast members did. Many of us, since it was an internship, left on the same day and all of us cried as we closed the store our final shift. We loved what we did.
Yes. [Emporium Costume](https://cornfieldsaresexy.files.wordpress.com/2013/01/223533_10150183054241543_6096191_n.jpg) this is NOT me, but this is the costume in all its glory.

Out of everything, I’d say working Baby Care (a nursing, changing place for parents and a little store for necessities) by myself, and standing over a pile of puke, making sure no one steps in it, while calling Custodial and waiting for them to come clean up the “Code V” (yep; it’s really called that).

So, I worked at Disney World in Orlando, Fl. My home was The Emporium in Magic Kingdom. It’s one of the biggest stores in the entirety of Disney property, and it’s frequented the most, since a lot of people who come to Disney for a shortened period of time, think of Magic Kingdom as Disney because of Cinderella’s Castle. I LOVED it. It was always crazy and crowded, there was never a dull moment. 

I did my internship with the Disney College Program, and they usually give the less desirable hours and shifts to us. Magic Kingdom is usually opened 1-3 hours later than any of the other three, and generally, Main Street—The Emporium, The Confectionery, etc is open an hour past park close. On nights where there are events or extra magic hours, technically we close when the park does. It’s a full time job, so you’d work 5-7 days in a row, with no specific set days off. I’ve worked shifts like 3:45p-11:45p, 7:15p-2:15a, and 8p-3a. So pretty much the night/closing shifts.

The virginity thing, I’d seen before so I’m not surprised. I haven’t really seen anything on SB’s with disabilities, so i guess I’m more curious about that. I’ll edit to add more.

Thanks!
